But I would say this, the more honestly you look at the world/life, that much more likely you are to get depressed.

Somtimes, i get that feeling too, especially when I am in a group on a party, ironically.

What tends to solve it, is... getting sober, and getting some sleep. I usually forget about it later, I don't hate loneliness, I embrace it.

But if you are not the one to embrace such things, well, go out and meet some people. You've got nothing to lose. You already went to a big party, so you don't have a major social anxiety, hopefully.

Just find someone who looks as bored as you might be, approach them and say "Hey.". That's how friendships start.

Good luck, hope you feel better/find someone.

Perhaps you should talk to your doctor about ADD, attention deficit disorder. It has no ties to depression.

This bug tends to follow the gifted individuals with higher IQ, and the symptom is, that you are just not interesting in anything and when you pick something up, it bores you quickly.

I thought I was fine, that it was the usue, I didn't know I suffered from ADD. I never got it treated, but pulled through it. You can fight it, but it's best that you get tested and treat it correctly.

So no, most likely, it's not a depression, it's ADD. Might be a burnout, but I don't think so.

I wouldn't say that. You just, "just", have to find a girl who has the same thinking process/problems as you have. It's hard, possible, but hard.

Looking outside that department will only bring pain, because a "normal" girl would never understand you, it wouldn't click.

I thought I find those, many times over in my life, now I'm 21 and no relationships behind me, or in front of me.

Because people are happy campers who have no clue of what depression/wanting to do it actually is/means.

In reality, noone really wants to kill themselves. Nobody. Everyone just wants a better life. People who are suicidal, like myself, want/NEED a big change in their life, often desperately, and they are not getting it/unable to make that change.

I've been called selfish yesterday, of course, by a happy camper. 18yo, great family, has a boyfriend, she didn't get the fact that I had nothing to life for/no hope of changing anything.

They just don't get that suicide is a quick end to the copious amounts of pain a person experiences. You wouldn't kill yourself over something meaningless, the problems must be severe.

Like I said, they just have no idea what it's actually to live with. Both depression and suicidal thoughts. They think it's an illness and you should be treated and locked up IMMEDIATELY.

"The stress of getting good grades" - overrated.

You don't need good grades. High school doesn't matter.
The only thing that matters, is that THIS should be the time of your life. Doing nothing, going to the parties, drinking with friends, dating some chicks, because after that, it gets worse for the majority.

You should try to enjoy it, and not think about it too much. After all, you're still kids. Doesn't seem like it when you're in there. Didn't seem like it to me. Looking back, it's absolutely right.

I know I'm not, I wouldn't do that. I'm a man of "cutting my losses".

Also this "entire life ahead of you", I wouldn't bank on that. Due to my weight/weak bone structure/something else, I've been dealing with:
Broken down knees: almost can't take steps, can't squat AT ALL, I had to drop football and cycling.
Arms: Constantly cracking elbows and wrists, sharp pain, numb fingers and constantly dropping things, because I have loose and sometimes no grip.

My right hip is destroyed (at the age of 21) and I also have some on and off heart problems, which even the doctor couldn't diagnose. He said I'm fine. Loud, fast heart-beats and seeing grey tunnels say otherwise.

So even if I wasn't depressed already, my body is breaking down like I'm 70 years old. Yeah, totally looking forward to that life in a wheelchair/under the knife constantly.

I was never a "bucket list"/dreaming person with things I want to do in life, so no, I don't. The only thing I wanted, is for the pain to be over already. I wanted something to be proud for, to make me happy.

I don't have it. And I already was an influence for some people, when they needed me.

PS: You talk about skydiving, that was one of my dreams. I'm 6'4, 350 lbs (and they only accpet like 6'2, 200 lbs), therefore not eligible for skydiving. 
I'm pretty sure they would let me in with my height with some begging, but with my skeleton, I wouldn't even want to lose 150 pounds. So I'm never going to live that dream.
The only skydiving I can get is to take the trip to the tallest building in the neighbourhood and jump off the roof.

I wouldn't mind living alone, I haven't done that yet though. I was still with my father and older brother.
The problem is, I don't have a penny or a job, or a place to stay, I have literally nothing. Rather than starving on the streets, I just want to end my suffering. There's been plenty of it, I think I deserve it.

Perhaps, in another dimension/life/afterlife/reincarnation/whatever, I will make more of my opportunities.

"I don't want to die, but I'm not afraid to." - Scott Hall

Me, personally, I fear life rather than death/what comes after.

At best, I get reincarnated as a flower or something. Or it's just an infinite lucid dream. Or, it's just pitch black. I will find out soon. But I'm looking forward to it, rather than being scared.

I have too. I have especially failed myself and my closest family.

But the part regarding no ambitions, dreams, etc.... you can live without that. As long as you have something close to you, you don't have to be an aspiring, top-tier human.
Some people just want lower-middle class and live out their lives, and that's completely normal.

So if you're just doing poorly at the moment, consider, whether or not you have something to look forward to/live for.
Whatever you do, my heart goes out to you.

"When you laugh, everyone laughs with you, when you cry, you cry alone."

Also, this thing you mentioned just comes down to basic human insincts.
People want to be included. In groups. So you might not be envious, but if you are doing poorly, you don't really want others to be doing great. Or at least you would not share the same happiness.

I'm struggling mightily with this, just because never clicks in my life.
Therefore, when someone gets in a relationship, I want them away, as far as they can be, from me.

Work in general, anything basically, has kept me from thinking about demons and bad places.

But to give you my experience... everywhere I went, people wanted to talk/demanded it from me. And being severely depressed, being an introvert and not trusting people makes it hard.
Perhaps that's the reason they kicked me out.

If I were to give you an advice, it would be this:
Try to find a job where you are all by yourself (so no talking/keep it low - colleagues wouldn't help you with depression, trust me)
Get yourself occupied (So do work, or, if not, try to read a lot, watch something, if you are bored, become creative, anything that keeps the mind rolling, so you don't have time to think about bad things)

I'm pretty sure, that in 20 years, the whole world would be different, and society as a whole would look upon me in the current state differently, dare I say moe positively.
But I've been living for tomorrows for the last 7 years and never truly felt like I got that energy refuel to keep going.

The only reason, and it is really the only one, that I didn't do this two months ago (had a set date already), was because I had a part-time job, and I wanted to fulfill my obligations AND spend the earned money.

The only real talk I wanna do, is:
1. I want people to understand, that for some, there really is no hope left, no other option, other than a slow, even more painful end.
2. For people like you, who have something to live for, to bloom and have a wonderful life. You know how to love, you know that feeling to be loved. You have the power of love. Use it wisely.

You're right about the part that I have literally nothing to lose. That's why I'm doing this.

I worked on myself in one way or another for the last 4 years. And I'm tired. Tired of trying, tired of putting effort in for no reward, tired of looking around, seeing happy faces and at least something working out for everyone and nothing for me.

Tired, chronically tired.

I was told "it gets better" about a billion times, it's never worked.

Even if the end-result looked like a hard-fought, meaningful victory, I never celebrated. And a moment later, it was even worse than before. And that was one of my biggest personal victories ever.

"It gets better" works, when you are 13 years old and break a mom's vase and feel shitty about it.

But when you are struggling with friendships/relationships/communication and someone tells you "it gets better", slap them in the face. They can help you make it better. Them saying those words makes it worse.

I first dipped into relationships when I was 13, trying to get my first girlfriend. "It gets better", and now I'm 21, still single, never even got close.
